text: The ability to generate new questions offers a way for AI systems to expand the challenges available for evaluation and learning. For visual questions, however, generating a correct answer is not enough: the answer may be known from the scene used to construct an image but not recoverable from the rendered pixels themselves. This makes automatic verification difficult, because checking only the underlying scene does not establish that the visual question is actually answerable. Using vision–language models to perform this check introduces a different problem: validity then depends on the capabilities of the models being evaluated. We introduce BlindLoop, a system in which coding agents propose visual questions and write two programs: one generates question instances and their expected answers, while the other solves them from the images alone. We check agreement across instances generated with different random seeds. We then investigate whether this approach supports continued growth of a question collection, whether agents can follow requests about which image regions their solving programs use, and whether they can use feedback about errors made by frontier models. We also analyze the verification procedure and evaluate the generated data through supervised fine-tuning. The resulting collections continue to grow across different question types, and agents usually follow requests about the size and shape of image regions used by their solving programs. Fine-tuning open-weight models on generated examples improves accuracy on held-out generated questions, with gains on several external benchmarks. Project page: https://theblindloop.github.io/
